MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  MAY 23, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to

MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan
City Council Member Absent:  Zuckerman

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton

Others Present:  Lisa Van Ingen Pope, Park and Activities Commission
  Robert Schachter, Planning Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The South Bay Assisteens led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 23, 2017
 B.  PLANNING  APPLICATION  NO. 08-17  (ENCROACHMENT  LICENSE
  AGREEMENT); APPLICANT:  RODGER KAUFMAN; LOCATION: 37 AURORA
  DRIVE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve PA-08-17 in the form of the
  Encroachment License Agreement for Rodger Kaufman, located at 37 Aurora
  Drive, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Planning Director Wahba noted
  that the encroachment fee is suggested to be waived due to the property owner
  maintaining all of the improvements in question.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested revisiting the encroachment permit fees for City
  properties in the future, but not impose one on this particular application.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ inquired if this item should be discussed City-
  wide. City Manager Prichard noted that this could be included for the Budget
  Study Session.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that this property serves no purpose except for
  the property owner, and if the City wishes to sell this area, an appraisal would
  be in order.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF referred to the retaining wall that has fallen into
  disrepair. She noted that Mr. Pisano, the next door neighbor, had to rebuild
  the wall and asked if he paid for those repairs. Mr. Pisano responded that he
  paid over $4,000 for the improvements.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Planning Director Wahba noted that
  this particular pathway was not maintained by the City and that Mr. Pisano
  took over this responsibility.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted her recollection that pedestrians desired
  access to this path. She further noted that the City might want to waive the
  annual fee in return for the property being maintained by the Applicant.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, City Attorney Davis noted that
  under the license agreement, proof of insurance and indemnification for the
  City is required. He further noted that any long-term thoughts about this
  property, i.e. vacation of a right-of-way, could be considered by the COUNCIL in
  the future, but it is a lengthy process.

  Rodger Kaufman, Applicant, commented that he has been working with
  Planning Director Wahba in an attempt to improve what was done several years
  ago. He noted that one has to walk down either of the driveways to access the
  trail.

  After further discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to waive the
  license fee in consideration of the Applicant building and maintaining the
  pathway and revise the agreement to reflect this amendment.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE PA-08-17 IN THE FORM OF AN ENCROACHMENT
  LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR RODGER KAUFMAN LOCATED AT 37
  AURORA DRIVE, TO INCLUDE A WAIVER OF FEES, AS AMENDED TO
  THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 23, 2017
 10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 33-16; APPLICANT:  MORLEY MENDELSON;
  LOCATION: 4 SILVER SADDLE LANE

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2396.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material). She
  noted that the Applicant has requested a postponement of his application.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that the COUNCIL previously took action on this
  matter to direct staff to prepare a resolution of approval, including conditions.
  He believed the best way to approach the Applicant’s request was to approve
  Resolution No. 2396, and if the Applicant does not wish to comply with the
  listed conditions, it could be rescinded at a future meeting and a new
  application would need to be filed.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, City Attorney Davis noted that
  either option would work, but it was his preference to postpone this item if the
  Applicant needs more time rather than bring the resolution back to the
  COUNCIL.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that the areas of concern were a non-compliant
  carport and a metal structure at the rear of the garage resulting in a violation of
  the 35’ setback requirement. He was adamant that a survey be conducted to
  determine the actual property lines. Finally, he stated that the COUNCIL had
  previously directed staff to outline all of the code violations, and if there was an
  encroachment over the property line, the application would go back to the
  Planning Commission regarding those structures built without a permit.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL suggested allowing the Applicant time to consider
  options, but if those structures were not removed, it would result in a denial by
  the COUNCIL. Senior Planner Naughton stated that the accessory building
  would either have to be relocated or removed to meet the setback requirements.

  Morley Mendelson, Applicant, referred to the height of the solar panels and was
  informed by his contractor that they would sit on an 18” base raising them
  beyond the fence which is unacceptable. He noted that he will have to cut back
  on the number of panels and amend his application.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO POSTPONE THIS ITEM UNTIL SUCH TIME AS THE APPLICANT
  CONDUCTS A LAND SURVEY AND ACCEPTS THE CONDITIONS
  IMPOSED BY THE COUNCIL OR SUBMIT A NEW APPLICATION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Zuckerman

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the

  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide

A.  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ reported on the South Bay Cities Council of
  Governments (SBCCOG) and County Water Resilience Working Group. She
  noted that they are seeking financing mechanisms for retention, maintenance
  and clean-up.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 23, 2017
 B.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL reported that the California Contract Cities
  Municipal Seminar had a good presentation on water and water conservation.

C.  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the following presentations are
  scheduled at the next COG meeting: 1) Recognition of Jim Goodhart, former
  COG Chair and Palos Verdes Estates Council Member; 2) Update from Los
  Angeles County Sheriff Jim McDonnell; and 3) The South Bay Broadband
  Feasibility Report.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL commented that Mr. Goodhart was an
  outstanding elected official and enjoyed working with him at the COG meetings,
  League of California Cities and other organizations. MAYOR ZERUNYAN
  concurred with COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL’S comments.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the new federal budget may be
  considering military base realignment which may put the Los Angeles Air Force
  Base at risk of closure. He noted that Supervisor Hahn is interested in looking
  at ways to protect the base and that he will contact her to discuss a strategy for
  its preservation.
